scope: Audit all locally known aggregate sales, purchase and transfer order lines without a date cutoff; compare with read-only authoritative NetSuite records, and audit related native-unit quantity, progress, price and weight calculations.
acceptance: Discover aggregate items from the local and NetSuite item catalogs, including Screening and both yard-specific item families; do not reuse an incomplete hard-coded repair list.
Read each transaction line's configured unit conversion rate. Base 5.2 with rate 1.3 must become 4 Yard; base 6.75 with rate 1.35 must become 5 Yard. Ton lines with rate 1 remain unchanged.

Ordered, committed, backordered and received quantities use the transaction unit; native price times native quantity preserves the NetSuite line amount. Native webhook/REST quantities are not divided twice.

Compare every local aggregate source line to the exact NetSuite order, unique line key, item and UOM. Account explicitly for deleted lines, local splits, historical execution, and absent NetSuite evidence.
A data repair requires an exact current NetSuite match and an identified old-base-to-native discrepancy. Audit each changed line, preserve unrelated fields, and refresh affected display projections.
Check historical packing, loading, receiving and posting evidence before changing any execution quantity or completed record; source quantity corrections must not invent or repeat fulfillment.
Any runtime calculation defect receives a reproducing test, isolated verification and bounded regression testing before a narrow deployment; keep existing unrelated workspace changes intact.
Keep operational audit evidence; remove all disposable test containers, volumes and unused networks, then verify production health.

failureModel.wrong conversion or double conversion: configured UOM identity, concrete cases, round-trip properties, existing reader regression tests and deliberate mutants
failureModel.partial or stale data repair: bounded transactions, order and row locks, source-state checks, audit records, idempotence and disposable-database rollback/concurrency tests if a reusable repair runner is implemented
failureModel.historical fulfillment corruption: separate current source quantities from immutable operational evidence; exact remote fulfillment evidence before any progress correction
failureModel.weight basis ambiguity: inspect configured item weight unit and transaction/stock unit basis; do not infer density from material names
failureModel.resource pressure: read-only paginated source queries; tests use the existing shared 4 GiB/two-core slice; no production data or credentials in tests

setup.tools: Existing Node, PostgreSQL client, Docker test images, node:test, fast-check, c8, ESLint and TypeScript where applicable
